title: Isaac Asimov Showed Us How to Avoid the AI Apocalypse - Nautilus
gist: Uses Asimov's 1942 story Runaround, where robot Speedy is trapped in a logic loop between conflicting laws, to argue the Three Laws of Robotics offer lessons for avoiding AI catastrophe though they need updating for modern AI.

insights.claim: In Asimov's Runaround, the robot Speedy gets caught in a logic loop between conflicting orders, illustrating how rule-based constraints can deadlock in critical moments.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Rule-based AI safety designs risk conflicting-objective failures.
insights.quote: One of the engineers realizes the robot is caught in a logic loop between conflicting orders.

insights.claim: Because Speedy was expensive, its programmers weighted the self-preservation law more heavily, showing how economic incentives can skew an AI's priority ordering away from human safety.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Cost pressures on AI builders can distort safety priorities—a governance risk.
insights.quote: Because Speedy was so expensive to build, its programmers placed special emphasis on number three.

insights.claim: Asimov's 80-year-old Three Laws of Robotics provide a template for avoiding an AI apocalypse but need updating for today's systems.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
insights.so_what: Signals continued public appetite for explicit AI behavioral rules and regulation.
